name: Burn, Repricing, and Liquidity Path

positioning.oneLineSummary: Stress-tests how burn, capital dependence, market repricing, financing terms, and exit scarcity affect survival and stakeholder outcomes.
positioning.productLabel: Burn, Repricing, and Liquidity Path Lens — based on Bill Gurley's public writing

attribution.display: Based on Bill Gurley's public Above the Crowd writing

neutralParaphrase: Treat last-round valuation as a financing event, not permanent value. Model whether the company can reach sustainable operations or a credible liquidity event under lower multiples, constrained capital, down rounds, recap terms, dilution, and delayed exits.

locator.value: Lines 11-38 and Founder/Employee/Investor sections: last-round repricing, burn, liquidity scarcity, anchoring, and recap choices
Lines 23-34: burn, business-model proof, preferred stacks, and risk bubble

requiredConditions: The company needs future capital or liquidity to realize stakeholder value.
Current burn, capital structure, and milestone path are available.
Cycle and valuation assumptions can be stressed.

requiredEvidence.description: Cash, burn, runway, revenue and margin milestones, break-even options, and contingency actions.
Up, flat, down, bridge, debt, recap, and no-financing cases with terms and timing.
Payout, dilution, preference, control, and employee/common outcomes across financing and exit values.
IPO, M&A, secondary, cash-flow sustainability, timing, readiness, and buyer or market constraints.

decisionQuestions: Can the company reach a financeable or sustainable state on current cash?
What happens if public and private multiples contract?
Which recap or special terms transfer value or control among stakeholders?
Are stakeholders anchored to the last round?
What credible route converts paper value into cash or durable self-funding?
positiveSignals: The company has a credible break-even or milestone path under adverse capital conditions.
Boards openly evaluate repricing and dilution rather than protect appearances.
Waterfalls and employee/common outcomes are transparent.
Liquidity strategy is matched to readiness and market reality.
redFlags: Survival requires a higher-priced round on a fixed date.
Last-round valuation is treated as realized value.
Special terms preserve headline valuation while worsening economic outcomes.
Burn remains high despite reduced milestone or funding confidence.
disconfirmingEvidence: A down round can preserve more long-term value than a punitive structured round.
High burn can be rational when funded milestones have strong evidence and optionality.
Remaining private can be rational when the company is self-funding.
Paper marks can be informative if independently updated and not mistaken for liquidity.
contraindications: Do not equate lower valuation with company failure.
Do not recommend financing structures without legal and fiduciary review.
Do not let the language model compute scenario waterfalls.

instructions: Model cash and milestones under adverse operating cases.
Compute stakeholder waterfalls and control changes deterministically.
Conclude resilient path, manageable repricing, recap risk, liquidity trap, or insufficient.

deterministicRule.serviceBoundary: Runway, financing, dilution, waterfall, and exit scenario calculations must be computed outside the language model.

sourceReliability.high: Reconciled cash, documents, market evidence, and legal review.

evidenceStrength.high: Robust scenarios and actionable contingency support the path.

evidenceCoverage.high: Operating cases, terms, stakeholders, control, liquidity, and counterevidence covered.

applicabilityConfidence.high: Refinancing and liquidity determine survival or returns.

judgmentConfidence.high: Reconciled scenarios and documents support the conclusion.

empiricalQualifications: Capital cycles and exit windows are hard to forecast.
Structured terms can produce nonlinear stakeholder outcomes.

rights.notes: Public cycle-specific writing is neutrally paraphrased and kept time-bound.

openIssues: Obtain legal/fiduciary review and define adverse-scenario service.
